You have to feel bad for Ben Simmons.

Not because he gave up an open layup in one of the biggest games of his career, but because his body gave up on him after trying to make a comeback in the league.

Simmons suffered a ruptured Achilles tendon just days before the Sacramento Kings open their regular season.

And just like that, another chapter of hope turns into absolute heartbreak.

It feels like a lifetime ago when Simmons was the undisputed future of basketball.

A 6'10" point guard with elite vision, lightning transition speed, and All-Defensive First Team chops.

He was dubbed THE next LeBron James, a generational marvel set to dominate for the next decade.

Then came the play in 2021. The passed-up dunk against the Hawks.

The fallout was loud, immediate, and unforgiving. The memes took over, and the internet turned his name into a punchline.

What most people missed through all the noise was a man fighting a losing battle with his own physical frame.

Multiple back surgeries, nerve damage, microdiscectomies, and endless rehab sessions. Every single time he tried to build momentum, his body put up a stop sign.

Stints with the Nets and Clippers faded away simply because his back wouldn't let him be Ben Simmons.

He could have walked away. He had the money and every reason to avoid the relentless scrutiny.

Instead, he spent a full year in silence rebuilding himself.

He grinded back to health, earned a spot with the Kings, and looked genuinely happy, sharp, and rejuvenated during preseason. He was finally ready to rewrite his story.

To put in all that unseen labor only for a freak Achilles tear to wipe it away days before opening night is nothing short of cruel.

Basketball fans love a slander train, but this isn't about stats or jump shots anymore.

This is a human story about a guy who kept trying to get back up, only to have the door slammed on him again.

Get well soon, Ben. The hustle to get back deserved a better ending 🙏🏼
